List each mock and say whether it is a *stateful* mock whose call-history/implementation could leak between tests. Show the exact beforeEach/afterEach/afterAll blocks present (with line numbers). 3. Git archaeology: find commit `a207b9a`. Run `git log -1 --format='%H %an <%ae> %ad %s' a207b9a` and `git show --stat a207b9a` and `git show a207b9a` (the diff). Report: who authored it, what it changed, and whether it moved clearAllMocks from beforeEach to afterEach (i.e. was it a compliance with an identical CodeRabbit finding?).

4. Search the PR review history for the two earlier clear-mocks findings. Use: `gh pr list --head feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui --json number` to get the PR number, then `gh api "repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/pulls/<N>/comments?per_page=100" --paginate --jq '.[] | select(.body|test("clearAllMocks|Clear Vitest mocks";"i")) | {id, path, line, created_at, body: .body[0:600]}'`. Also fetch replies: `gh api "repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/pulls/<N>/comments?per_page=100" --paginate --jq '.[] | select(.in_reply_to_id != null) | {id, in_reply_to_id, user: .user.login, body: .body[0:800]}'` and find any reply that declined or accepted a clear-mocks finding. Quote the decline reasoning verbatim if found.

Report terse findings with exact line numbers and verbatim quotes. Do not write any files.

content.text:
I have everything. Here are the findings.

## Bottom line

The finding is a **provable no-op in all five files**. It is also **factually wrong about two of them** — `footerNavColumn/index.test.tsx` and `useUiCopy.test.tsx` have **no `beforeEach`/`afterEach` at all**, so there is no `vi.clearAllMocks()` to "move." And it is the **third** iteration of the same finding on PR #59; the second one was complied with rather than argued, in the user's own commit `a207b9a`.

---

## Q1 — Per-file analysis

Vitest **3.2.7**. `vi.clearAllMocks()` → `.mockClear()` on every registered mock: clears `mock.calls`/`instances`/`contexts`/`results` only. It does **not** reset implementations or return values (that's `mockReset`). So a `mockReturnValue` set in test N survives into test N+1 either way — the only thing at stake is call history.

### `overrides/app/components/footer/index.test.tsx` (cited L140-143) — has beforeEach
```
 12  vi.mock('app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon', () => ({
 13    ZimmIcon: () => null,          ← plain arrow fn, NOT vi.fn() → not in the mock registry
 14  }));
 16  vi.mock('@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-multi-site', () => ({
 17    default: vi.fn(),              ← stateful
 18  }));
 20  vi.mock('app/hooks/useContentfulClient', () => ({
 21    useContentfulClient: vi.fn(),  ← stateful
 22  }));
139  describe('FooterContainer', () => {
140    beforeEach(() => {
141      vi.clearAllMocks();
142      mockSite('ZimmermannAU');
143    });
```
Only hook block in the file. Two stateful mocks, plus a per-test `vi.fn()` for `getEntries` (L150, 160, 168, 177, 190, 204, 214) — created fresh inside each test. **Zero `toHaveBeenCalled*` / `mock.calls` assertions in the whole file.** No test reads call history, so clearing it before vs. after a test is unobservable. The one boundary asymmetry — `beforeEach` also wipes anything accumulated during the preceding `describe('scopeToRegion')` (L64-110) — is empty in practice: those are pure-function tests that never invoke a mock. **No-op.**

### `overrides/app/components/footer/footerNavColumn/index.test.tsx` (cited L14-21) — NO hooks
```
 14  vi.mock('app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon', () => ({
 18    ZimmIcon: (props: { 'aria-label'?: string; 'aria-hidden'?: boolean }) => (
 19      <span aria-label={props['aria-label']} aria-hidden={props['aria-hidden']} />
 20    ),
 21  }));
```
The **only** `vi.*` call in the file, and its factory returns a **plain arrow function component, not a `vi.fn()`** — it never enters the mock registry, so `clearAllMocks()` has literally nothing to iterate. No `beforeEach`/`afterEach`/`beforeAll`/`afterAll` anywhere (L1-89). Nothing to move; adding a hook would clear nothing. **Provable no-op.**

### `overrides/app/hooks/useUiCopy.test.tsx` (cited L2-25) — NO hooks
Whole file is 25 lines. One `vi.*` call:
```
 15    const contextValue = { t: vi.fn().mockReturnValue('S’inscrire'), isLoading: true };
```
Created inside the **second and last** test, scoped to it, never referenced again, and no assertion reads its call history (L22 asserts the *return value* via `result.current.t(...)`). No hooks at all. **Provable no-op** — and there is no subsequent test for state to leak into.

### `overrides/app/components/uiCopyProvider/index.test.tsx` (cited L28-31) — has beforeEach
```
 12  vi.mock('app/hooks/useContentful', () => ({
 13    useContentfulEntries: vi.fn(),   ← stateful, the only registered mock
 14  }));
 28  describe('UiCopyProvider', () => {
 29    beforeEach(() => {
 30      vi.clearAllMocks();
 31    });
```
Every one of the 5 tests calls `mockUseContentfulEntries.mockReturnValue(...)` itself (L34, 46, 58, 67, 76) before rendering, and `mockReturnValue` overwrites — so no implementation can leak. Zero `toHaveBeenCalled*` assertions. **No-op.** Note the `beforeEach` contains *nothing but* the clear, so "keep `beforeEach` for per-test setup" would leave an empty hook that has to be deleted — the suggestion doesn't fit this file's shape.

### `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmSubscribeSection/index.test.tsx` (cited L77-82) — has beforeEach
```
 77  describe('ZimmSubscribeSection', () => {
 78    beforeEach(() => {
 79      vi.clearAllMocks();
 80      mockHook();
 81      mockUseUiCopy.mockReturnValue({ t: (_key: string, fallback: string) => fallback, isLoading: false });
 82    });
```
This is the only one of the five with call-history assertions — and all three targets are **fresh `vi.fn()`s created inside their own test**, so cross-test leakage is structurally impossible:
- L138 `const handleEmailSubmit = vi.fn();` → L145 `expect(handleEmailSubmit).toHaveBeenCalledWith('shopper@example.com')`
- L149 `const handleModalSubmit = vi.fn();` → L155 `toHaveBeenCalledWith('Jane', 'Smith')`
- L193 `const closeModal = vi.fn();` → L199 `toHaveBeenCalled()`

The module-level mocks (`zimmIcon` L12-16 — again a plain arrow fn, not `vi.fn()`; `zimmSubscribeModal` L23-39 — plain fn; `useSubscribeSection` L45-47 — `vi.fn()`; `useUiCopy` L53-55 — `vi.fn()`) are re-stubbed by `mockHook()`/`mockUseUiCopy.mockReturnValue` in `beforeEach` on every test, and none has its call history asserted. **No-op.**

**Verdict on Q1:** moving the clear to `afterEach` changes observable behaviour in **none** of the five suites. The pattern the finding warns about (a `beforeEach` clear followed by a return-value stub, where moving the clear would be equivalent) holds in all three files that have a `beforeEach` — and the other two have no hook to move.

---

## Q2 — Repo-wide practice + config

**Config is decisive-adjacent but not decisive**: `vitest.config.ts` sets **none** of `clearMocks` / `mockReset` / `restoreMocks`. Full `test` block, verbatim:
```ts
  test: {
    globals: true,
    environment: 'jsdom',
    setupFiles: ['./vitest.setup.ts'],
    include: ['overrides/**/*.test.ts', 'overrides/**/*.test.tsx'],
    passWithNoTests: true,
  },
```
`vitest.setup.ts` is one line: `import '@testing-library/jest-dom';`. So no global auto-clear — the per-file hooks are the only mechanism. (Both files are Tier 1 anyway.)

**16 test files total. Counts:**

| Pattern | Count | Files |
|---|---|---|
| `beforeEach(vi.clearAllMocks())` | **5** | `footer/index.test.tsx:141`, `zimmSubscribeSection/index.test.tsx:79`, `uiCopyProvider/index.test.tsx:30`, `hooks/useCountryConfig.test.ts:19`, `hooks/useContentfulClient.test.ts:31` |
| `afterEach(vi.clearAllMocks())` | **2** | `zimmTextInput/zimmTextInput.css.test.ts:22-24`, `hooks/useZimmTextInputState.test.ts:16-18` |
| `afterEach(vi.restoreAllMocks())` | **1** | `utils/resolveByRegion.test.ts:73-75` (paired with `beforeEach` at L69-70 doing `vi.spyOn(console,'warn')` — the one file where the hook is genuinely load-bearing) |
| Neither | **8** | `footerNavColumn/index.test.tsx`, `hooks/useUiCopy.test.tsx`, `hooks/useSubscribeSection.test.ts`, `hooks/useZimmModal.test.tsx`, `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`, `theme/fontFace.test.tsx`, `theme/index.test.tsx`, `utils/safeHref.test.ts` |

So **`beforeEach` is the repo majority, 5 vs 2** — and 8 of 16 files do neither. Of the 8 "neither" files, 5 contain no `vi.fn`/`vi.mock`/`vi.spyOn` at all; `fontFace.test.tsx` was explicitly cleared by CodeRabbit (see below).

The rule CodeRabbit quotes is **`.claude/rules/testing.md:67`**, verbatim, a single line:
> `- Use `beforeEach` for setup; clear mocks with `vi.clearAllMocks()` after each test.`

Worth noting that line names **both** hooks, and "after each test" is the phrase CodeRabbit leans on. Tier 1 governance file (`.claude/rules/`), so tightening the wording to "where there are mocks or state to reset" is itself a gated change.

---

## Q3 — Commit `a207b9a`

```
a207b9a242c390f1043d2411abe58ab825fae65b
Marcel Angelo Navarro <marcel.a.n.navarro@accenture.com>
Sat Aug 22 01:22:35 2026 +0800
test(zimm-text-input): add the conventional beforeEach/afterEach hooks
```
**Authored by you.** Single file, `overrides/app/theme/components/zimmTextInput.test.ts`, +15/-2 (that file is now `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmTextInput/zimmTextInput.css.test.ts` after the co-location move).

It did **not** move `clearAllMocks` from `beforeEach` to `afterEach` — the file had **neither** hook. It *added both*, converting `const base = {...}` to a `let` reinitialised per test and adding an `afterEach` clear:
```ts
+// .claude/rules/testing.md asks for beforeEach setup and vi.clearAllMocks() after each test.
+// The resolvers here are pure and this file mocks nothing, so these hooks are a convention
+// baseline rather than load-bearing isolation — kept so the file matches the rule as written
+// and stays correct if a mock is ever introduced.
+let base: ZimmTextInputStyleProps;
+
+beforeEach(() => {
+  base = { inverse: false, disabled: false, hasError: false, focused: false, filled: false };
+});
+
+afterEach(() => {
+  vi.clearAllMocks();
+});
```
The commit body states the reasoning plainly: *"This file's resolvers are pure and it mocks nothing, so the hooks reset no observable state — added for consistency with the rule as written rather than for isolation."* That file still contains **zero mocks** today (only `vi.` occurrence is the `clearAllMocks` itself, L23).

**So yes — `a207b9a` is compliance with a materially identical CodeRabbit finding, conceded after arguing it was a no-op and being overruled on the rule's unconditional wording.**

---

## Q4 — PR review history: this is finding #3

PR is **#59** (open, `feat(footer): SFCC-55 global footer UI — shell, layout, and ui-kit component structure`). PR #55 is the closed predecessor and has **zero** clear-mocks comments. Four related findings on #59, in order:

**1. `useZimmTextInputState.test.ts` — 2026-08-20T18:38:49Z (id 3824358472), Minor.** *"Clear Vitest mocks after each test. Add `afterEach(() => vi.clearAllMocks())`."* → **Accepted without argument.** Your reply (id 3831356839): "Fixed in `7e1c081`." That commit added exactly the suggested `afterEach` block. That file *does* have real `vi.fn()`s (L32, 42, 57), so this one was arguably legitimate.

**2. `theme/fontFace.test.tsx` — 2026-08-21T06:17:25Z (id 3827758554), Minor.** → **DECLINED, and CodeRabbit withdrew it.** Your decline (id 3831565216), verbatim in relevant part:

> "Not changing this. The file already handles test isolation, and the specific additions would not do anything here. […] On `vi.clearAllMocks()`: there is nothing to clear. The only mock in the file is a module-level `vi.mock` of `ssr-namespace-paths`, which is hoisted and returns static values. There are no spies accumulating calls, so the call would be a no-op."

CodeRabbit's response (id 3831572189): *"I withdraw this finding. The existing setup keeps each asset-resolution branch explicit… `vi.clearAllMocks()` would not change test behaviour."* — and it **recorded a learning** for the file.

**3. `theme/components/zimmTextInput.test.ts` — 2026-08-21T16:34:51Z (id 3831972405), Minor.** → **Declined, then overruled, then complied.** Your decline (id 3832191582):

> "Both hooks would be provable no-ops in this file: It contains zero `vi.*` calls, so `vi.clearAllMocks()` has nothing to clear. `base` is a frozen object literal that is only ever spread into calls (`{...base, focused: true}`) and never mutated… `.claude/rules/testing.md` asks for `beforeEach` setup and `clearAllMocks` where there is state or mocks to reset — the point of the guideline is isolation between tests, and there is nothing here that leaks. Adding both would read as if this file had shared state to defend against, which is the opposite of what is true."

CodeRabbit refused (id 3832194970), and this is the key precedent for the current finding:

> "the hooks have no current runtime effect. The test file does not create mocks, and it does not mutate `base`. **However, the repository-specific rule is unconditional:** 'Use `beforeEach` for setup; clear mocks with `vi.clearAllMocks()` after each test.' It does not restrict these hooks to tests with mocks or mutable setup state. I will keep this finding open because the requested change is required by the stated test convention."

You then complied (id 3832279042): *"Done in a207b9a … You're right that the rule in `.claude/rules/testing.md` is stated without qualification, and consistency with the convention as written is worth more than the argument."*

**4. The current finding — two comments, both 2026-08-24, both unanswered.**
- id **3841007258**, 05:58:12Z, on `useUiCopy.test.tsx#L25` — flagged **🟠 Major** (an escalation; every prior one was Minor). Suggests adding `afterEach` inside `describe('useUiCopy')`.
- id **3841133765**, 06:28:34Z, on `footer/index.test.tsx#L143` — **🟡 Minor**, a *consolidated* finding naming 4 files in its `<consolidated_sites>` block (footer, footerNavColumn, useUiCopy, uiCopyProvider). `zimmSubscribeSection#L77-82` appears **only** inside the "🤖 Prompt for AI Agents" body, not in the structured site list — so it's a 5th target smuggled in via prose.

Note the two overlap: `useUiCopy.test.tsx` is flagged twice, at Major and Minor severity, 30 minutes apart. **Neither has a reply yet** — so per AGENTS.md's CodeRabbit-response rule, both need an in-thread reply regardless of whether you change the code.

---

## What this means for your reply

The precedent cuts both ways and you should decide deliberately rather than by default:

- The **fontFace** exchange establishes CodeRabbit *will* withdraw a clear-mocks finding when shown the mock is not a `vi.fn()`/spy with accumulating state. That argument applies **exactly and more strongly** to `footerNavColumn` and `useUiCopy` — the former's only `vi.mock` factory returns a plain arrow component, and the latter's single `vi.fn()` lives in the file's last test.
- The **zimmTextInput** exchange establishes it will *not* withdraw on a "provable no-op" argument alone, because `testing.md:67` is unconditional.

The distinguishing move available to you: the current finding asks to **move** something, and in two of the five named files there is **nothing to move** — a factual error, not a judgement call. For the three that do have `beforeEach(clearAllMocks)`, the honest position is that it's a stylistic no-op and the repo majority is 5-to-2 in favour of the current `beforeEach` form, so complying here would make three files inconsistent with `useCountryConfig.test.ts:19` and `useContentfulClient.test.ts:31`, which the finding doesn't mention. If you'd rather settle this permanently, the root cause is the unqualified wording at `.claude/rules/testing.md:67` — but that's a Tier 1 governance file and needs both squad leads plus the Integration lead.
